stages.name: Small-workload fit assessment
stages.text: Understand readiness, simpler alternatives, risks and operator needs before choosing a platform.
features: Risks, operator needs and a scoped next step
stages.callout: A standalone assessment, not a platform installation. No upgrade required.

stages.name: Hands-on Kubernetes pilot
stages.best: Start with one node. Expand as your needs grow.
stages.text: Start with a single-node Kubernetes deployment and local storage for non-critical workflows that can accommodate scheduled downtime, such as build servers, self-hosted analytics, or internal automation. Work alongside your engineer, with a path to expand to high availability later.
features: Basic backups, restore validation and an operating runbook
stages.callout: For container-ready or readily containerized workloads within an agreed scope. A single node has no failover, so workflows must also tolerate unplanned outages. Expansion to high availability is scoped separately. No complex migration or regulated production data.

stages.name: Small Private Platform Launch
stages.best: Network storage. Tested recovery. Ready to grow.
stages.text: Build the foundation for a resilient platform. Networked storage, automated off-node backups, tested recovery, and multi-node-ready networking prepare your workloads for future high availability.
features: Networked or shared storage and multi-node-ready networking
Automated off-node backups and tested restores
Repeatable delivery, secure access and monitoring
stages.callout: Scoped for 1–2 suitable applications with a named client operator. Includes defined stabilization and defect correction. This is the foundation for high availability; network storage alone does not provide failover. Redundant infrastructure and validated failover are scoped under Resilient.

stages.name: Resilient Platform Launch
stages.text: Put high availability into operation with redundancy across the control plane, application placement and storage, tested against agreed failure scenarios and recovery objectives.
features: Launch storage, networking, backup and operating foundations
Redundant control plane, application placement and storage
Failover and recovery testing against agreed acceptance criteria
stages.callout: Resilience follows agreed recovery objectives and acceptance tests. Scope and complexity determine the price, not simply node count.

addons.name: GPU enablement for AI workflows
addons.text: Enable GPUs for a defined workflow, including scheduling, access controls, integration and validation—for example, deploying a private AI inference service on your own hardware.

addons.name: Advanced database and recovery
addons.text: Database-specific replication, migrations or tighter recovery targets beyond your package’s included backups and recovery validation. Launch already includes automated off-node backups and tested restores.

addons.name: Advanced CI/CD
addons.text: Multi-environment or complex delivery integration beyond the included deployment path.

addons.name: Advanced secure-access integration
addons.text: Specialist access integration beyond the launch security baseline, such as VPN access, zero trust integration, or SSO-based access controls.

addons.name: KubeVirt / legacy-VM assessment
addons.text: Review compatibility, dependencies and recovery. Migration implementation is quoted separately.

addons.name: Custom platform engineering
addons.text: Additional apps or migrations from $5,000 per app; specialist scope assessed separately. Included apps are not billed twice.

addons.name: On-site implementation
addons.text: Local installation, validation and paired handoff. Time and travel quoted separately; remote work is an option.

support.name: Handoff only
support.text: Your qualified operator or MSP takes over after included stabilization. Complete documentation and operating handoff.

support.name: Advisory
support.text: Scheduled review and 1–2 hours of advice for a capable operator. No hands-on maintenance or operational ownership.

support.name: Scheduled Platform Care
support.text: Agreed updates, health and backup reviews, maintenance and reporting for one named environment within written capacity limits.
